limits.guard_coverage: The guard wraps the global fetch of the agent process only. node:https, node:http and child processes are NOT covered.
limits.key_scope: The key exists only in the environment of the agent process (spawn env) and is not passed to agent evidence. Engineering tools run under bwrap --clearenv with an environment declared as not inherited. Read from the code, not measured in a run.
limits.protected_comparison: Protected cases compare with isDeepStrictEqual (key order of an object is irrelevant; undefined, NaN, -0 and the type are distinguished).
limits.cap_effect: Hitting the cap is a datum apart (cap_reached, analysis.by_arm): the original adapter proof is kept untouched and the outcome is the protected tests on the rebuilt final file plus the product verifier.
limits.real_path_never_exercised: The real path (network, the key, `hseos memory promote` in a TTY) was never exercised by this script: no real call, no real key and no TTY promotion took place while it was written or tested.
limits.rehearsal_scope: The rehearsal uses a programmed fake model and only proves the plumbing (boxes, retrieval, meter, receipts, stop rules); it says nothing about what the real model does.
limits.credit_declared_not_verified: The credit (--credit-usd) is declared by the operator from the console; the script does not verify it.
limits.cost_is_estimate: The cost against the US$ 3.00 ceiling is the script estimate from the declared price (no cache discount), not an invoice.
failure_paths_covered: response that is not an event stream (usage unreadable)
request cut by the timeout (stops at the first occurrence)
request cap reached (original proof kept, counted apart)
observed model or origin diverging from the declared one
count-independent proof checks failing on a capped run
promotions missing, edited manifest, wrong sha256, wrong operator, control box altered or promoted
missing or wrong confirmation, price, credit, key, relative root, heavy-run ancestor or unreadable process ancestry
failure_paths_not_covered: real provider HTTP errors (4xx, 5xx, 429 rate limit) and network or DNS failure
a stream truncated in the middle of an event
key revoked or credit exhausted in the middle of the campaign
the provider changing the model behind the same dated name
the campaign process killed (SIGKILL) in the middle of a run, and any resume
the interactive `hseos memory promote` flow itself (TTY, confirmation prompt)
divergence between the script estimate and the console cost
limits.product_files_static: PRODUCT_FILES is a static list derived from an execution trace in a fixture run, not recomputed. 9 files reachable by a static require from hseos-cli.js are not in it (governed-action, entrypoint-adapters, agent-environment/dap, dap-host, framing, browser-contract, legacy-mcp-server, mcp-transport, mcp-protocol), probably lazy requires outside the agent run path; this is not proved.
limits.hash_fail_closed_files: package.json and tools/cli/command-manifest.json are in the hash, so changing either invalidates the confirmation (fail-closed).
limits.hash_not_covered: The hash does not cover node_modules, the Node version or the content of the real project.db (only the sha256 of its copy is recorded).
limits.heavy_run_detection: The heavy-run detection is a regex over the process command line and can wrongly BLOCK a legitimate run (BLOCKED with no cost).
limits.promoted_id_format: The format of the promoted_id written by `hseos memory promote` in a real TTY was not exercised; verify-promotions expects `<memory_id>:promoted` as the product store produces it in the API path.
limits.timeout_policy: A request cut by the timeout is charged at the pessimistic cost, written to the log and STOPS the campaign at the first occurrence (STOPPED: timeout). This differs from v3, which left the decision to the owner.
limits.measures: Does not measure usefulness in real work; one model, one provider, n = 5 per task and condition; "almost certain by construction" caveat of the protocol stands.
